classification_reasoning: CURRENT_STATE_OVER_HISTORY's own logic was never falsified -- on every probe where it had >=2 surviving items to act on (SUP3 and all 3 R4 controls), it behaved exactly as specified: correct state-key detection (verified separately at $0 by tests/test_state_supersession.py, 11/11), correct non-collapse of genuinely distinct entities (0/3 false supersession on R4), and a correct, safe refusal to guess on SUP3's metadata-timestamp tie rather than risk a wrong split. The FAIL is explained entirely by a harness-precondition failure: in 8 of 9 R1/R2/R3 probes, Mem0 1.0.6's own write-time ADD/UPDATE/DELETE reconciliation fully consolidated the sequential same-key state updates into a single surviving memory (keeping only the newest text, discarding the rest) BEFORE the read-side mechanism ever received multiple competing items to disambiguate. This is not an IMPLEMENTATION_FAILURE (state_supersession.py behaved correctly given its inputs), not a READER_FAILURE (the reader correctly answered from whatever it was given), not JUDGE_NOISE (both passes agreed on every probe, 0 disputed), and not a SELECTION_ARTIFACT in the pejorative sense of a poorly-chosen probe topic -- the topics were fine; the probes' TURN SPACING was the flaw: each state-changing probe packed 2-3 closely-related statements into immediate adjacency with nothing else in the store, which is close to the easiest possible case for Mem0's own 'existing memories' comparison to recognize the relation and choose UPDATE over ADD. Real LongMemEval conversations separate related statements with many unrelated intervening turns across sessions, diluting that comparison -- V1's compact synthetic probes did not reproduce that separation.
new_finding_not_previously_recorded: Mem0 1.0.6's write-time UPDATE path can silently overwrite metadata.timestamp on an EXISTING memory to match a LATER, unrelated add() call's timestamp, even when that existing memory's own TEXT is left unchanged (observed on SUP3_RELATIONSHIP_STATUS: 'Got engaged to my partner' kept its original wording but its stored metadata.timestamp was rewritten from 2021-08-05 to 2023-02-14, matching the second ingest call). This means evidence_times, the field TEMPORAL_ANCHOR_AT_CONTEXT (Ledger Entries A/B) and CURRENT_STATE_OVER_HISTORY (Ledger Entry F) both depend on as their sole recency signal, is not always a reliable record of a memory's own original observation time on this Mem0 version -- it can be silently touched by a LATER, textually-unrelated write. CURRENT_STATE_OVER_HISTORY's tie-safe fallback happened to absorb this cleanly in SUP3 (both items showed the same date, so it declined to guess), but a future probe where this corruption produces a WRONG order rather than a tie would not be caught the same way. Recorded as a new, independent infrastructure risk, not yet its own ledger entry pending further characterization.
repair_justification: The flaw is a single, deterministic, uniformly-applied harness precondition (probe turns packed with no separating content), not per-probe wording tuned to a judge, not gold-aware, and not a host-specific exception-handling hack. The fix (insert a fixed, small number of unrelated filler turns between each pair of state-changing turns, identical rule applied to all 9 R1/R2/R3 probes, R4 left untouched since it was never broken) is generalizable and matches the real regime's structural property (related facts separated by other conversation) rather than reverse-engineering Mem0's judge/update-decision wording. One retest only, per the $0.30 repair budget.
